Rashi on Eruvin 80a:11:1.hebrew: בריה דבת יעקב - אביו לא היה הגון, לפיכך לא הזכירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:11:1.english: The son of the daughter of Ya’akov - His father was not worthy; therefore, [the Gemara] did not mention him.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:11:2.english: Take a roundabout route - Extend the journey on my account for his sake:

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:11:3.english: And go to the Ladder of Tyre - By way of the highway of Tyre.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:11:4.hebrew: <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> חייא קאי כרב בתחומין. וגבי חצירות — טעמא דרב משום דכיון דקאסר עליה, גמר ומקני ואין צריך זכייה. <abbr title="ואף על גב">ואע"ג</abbr> <abbr title="דמתניתין">דמתני'</abbr> פליגא עליה דרב — רב תנא ופליג:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:11:4.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya holds in accordance with Rav regarding [Shabbat] boundaries. And with regard to courtyards, Rav's reasoning is that since [the other neighbor] restricts him, he wholeheartedly transfers [possession], and there is no need to confer possession. And even though the Mishnah disagrees with Rav, Rav is a tanna and [has the authority to] disagree.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:17:1.english: Is there anyone who disputes [it] - Do we find that anyone disagrees with him?

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:18:1.hebrew: טורזינא - נכרי היה, ממונה על כלי זיין העשויין לשמירת העיר להלחם על הצרים, ודר בעיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:18:1.english: Turzina - He was a gentile, appointed over weapons designated for guarding the city to fight against enemies, and he lived in the city.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:1:1.hebrew: ואין טועמין מפירותיה - דאי לאו דפלחוה, לא הוו פרשי מינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:1:1.english: And they do not taste of its fruit - For were it not that they worshiped it, they would not abstain from it.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:22:1.hebrew: הא דאסר - על בני המבוי, לא בעינן דעתיה. ומתניתין — בדלא אסר, כגון חצר שבין שני מבואות, ורגילה עם זה ולא עם זה:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:22:1.english: This [case is where] he prohibits - [If he would prohibit] the residents of the alleyway, we do not require his consent. And the Mishnah [i.e., the baraita] — [deals with a case] where he does not prohibit [them], such as a courtyard that is between two alleyways, and is accustomed [to merge] with this one and not with that one.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:23:1.english: So too, it is reasonable - That Shmuel concedes [in a case] where he does not prohibit [them].

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:23:2.english: And he did not join - He does not want [to join] and intends to render [carrying] forbidden to them.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:2:1.hebrew: נצרפי - שם ע"ז שהיתה באותה מדינה:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:2:1.english: Nitzrefei - The name of an idol that was in that country.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:4:1.hebrew: צריך להודיע - אם חפצין בכך, שמא מקפידין בעירובין. ואמר (בפ"ק): ״המקפיד על עירובו — אינו עירוב״, שעינו צרה באותה פת ליתן לחביריו. אבל משלו — אין צריך להודיעו, דזכין לו לאדם שלא בפניו:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:4:1.english: He must inform [them] - [To know] if they desire this, lest they are particular about the eruv. And it was said (in the first chapter): “One who is particular about his eruv, [it] is not an eruv,” for he is begrudging with that bread to give [it] to his fellows. But [if the barrel is] of his own, he does not need to inform him, for one may act to a person's benefit in his absence.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:6:1.hebrew: הכא תנן - בעירובי חצירות, ומזכה להן:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:6:1.english: Here we learned - With regard to courtyard eiruvs, [the Mishnah teaches]: “And he confers possession to them.”

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:6:2.hebrew: הכא לא תנן - בעירובי תחומין קתני לקמן (עירובין דף פב.) כיצד משתתפין בתחומין וכו', ולא קתני ומזכה להן:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:6:2.english: Here we did not learn - With regard to eruvei techumin [a joining of Shabbat boundaries], it teaches below (Eruvin 82a): "How do they join for [Shabbat] boundaries, etc.", and it does not teach: "and he confers possession to them."

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:7:1.hebrew: שהלכה לבית המרחץ - מבעוד יום, חוץ לתחום עירה, וחשכה לה, ואסר לה לחזור:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:7:1.english: Who went to the bathhouse - While it was still day, outside the Shabbat boundary of her town, and night fell upon her, and it was forbidden for her to return.

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:8:1.hebrew: ר' חייא - בבלי היה, כדאמרינן במסכת סוכה (דף כ.): עלו ר' חייא ובניו ויסדוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 80a:8:1.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya - He was a Babylonian, as we say in Tractate Sukkah (20a): "Rabbi Ḥiyya and his sons went up and established it."

Rashi on Eruvin 80a:9:1.english: And a dilemma was raised before them - This is our reading.

Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:14:1.hebrew: אמר רב נחמן נקיטינן אחד עירובי תחומין ואחד שיתופי מבואות צריך לזכות - וכן הלכה. וכן פסק בשאלתות בפרשת ויהי בשלח, דכולם צריכין לזכות: עירובי תחומין, וחצירות, ושיתופי מבואות, ועירובי תבשילין. ואע"ג דבעי רב נחמן "עירובי תבשילין מאי" — הא מסיק אביי דלא שמיע ליה דשמואל; דאי שמיע ליה, לא הוה מיבעיא ליה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:14:1.english: Rav Naḥman said: We hold based on tradition that both [regarding] the joining of Shabbat boundaries and the merging of alleyways, it is necessary to confer possession - And so is the halakhah. And so [Rav Aḥai] ruled in the She'iltot in Parashat Vayeḥi Beshallaḥ, that for all of them it is necessary to confer possession: the joining of Shabbat boundaries, and [the joining of] courtyards, and the merging of alleyways, and the joining of cooked foods [eiruv tavshilin]. And even though Rav Naḥman raised the dilemma, "What [is the law regarding] a joining of cooked foods?", behold, Abaye concludes that he had not heard that [teaching] of Shmuel; for had he heard it, he would not have raised this dilemma.

Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:20:1.hebrew: אתו לקמיה דרב יהודה אמר להו הכי אמר שמואל אשתו של אדם כו' - ואם תאמר: ואמאי לא מייתי מדרב יהודה, דאמר בריש כדר (לע. ל דף סד.) משמיה דשמואל: "שכירו ולקיטי של נכרי נותן עירובו ודיו", וכל שכן אשתו — והוה מייתי מנכרי אנכרי? ויש לומר: דאשתו אאשתו ניחא ליה לאתויי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:20:1.english: They came before Rav Yehuda, [who] said to them: Shmuel said as follows: "A man’s wife..." etc. - And if you say: Why did he not cite from [that which] Rav Yehuda said at the beginning of [the chapter] Hadar (above, 64a) in the name of Shmuel: "A gentile's hired worker and resident laborer gives his eiruv and that suffices" — and all the more so his wife! — and [thus] he would have cited [a proof] from a gentile to a gentile?! And one can say: It was preferable to him to cite [from] a wife to a wife.

Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:24:1.hebrew: רגיל אין שאינו רגיל לא - דרגיל אסר, כמו פתח הרגיל, אבל שאינו רגיל אינו אוסר. ונוטלים שיתופו בעל כרחו דקאמר — היינו של בעל הבית, אבל דעת אשתו צריך. ואף על גב דאסיקנא דאשתו של אדם מערבת שלא מדעתו, אין ללמוד מכאן שתוכל לזכות לבני המבוי ולבני חצר לתת פת עבורם; נהי דבשביל עצמה יכולה ליתן שלא מדעת בעלה, אין לה כח לזכות לשכיניה שלא מדעת. וצריך ליזהר שלא תזכה האשה לשכיניה כשאין בעלה בעיר. ואף על גב דאם כל אחד ואחד נותן פת נראה דשרי, אפילו לא אסרי אהדדי, כל זמן שלא מיחה הבעל, דמסתמא לא קפיד — מכל מקום אין לסמוך על זה לענין שתוכל לזכות לאחרים. ואם אין הבעל זה אשה בעיר אלא בני ביתו, צריך לדקדק אם יכולין לערב בני ביתו בלא רשות משל בעל הבית; דהא בסמוך [עמוד ב] תנן: ניתוספו עליהן מוסיף וצדיך להודיע, וכשכלה האוכל נמי קתני דצריך להודיע ממין אחר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:24:1.english: "[If he was] accustomed, yes; [if he was] not accustomed, no" - For one who is accustomed [to participate] causes a prohibition, like an accustomed doorway; but one who is not accustomed does not cause a prohibition. And that which it says, "they take his contribution to the merging of alleyways against his will" — that is [against the will] of the homeowner, but the consent of his wife is required. And even though we concluded that a person's wife may establish an eiruv without his knowledge, one cannot learn from here that she is able to transfer ownership to the residents of the alleyway and to the residents of the courtyard [by] giving bread on their behalf. Granted that on her own behalf she can give [bread] without her husband's knowledge, [yet] she does not have the power to transfer ownership to her neighbors without [his] knowledge. And one must be careful that the woman does not transfer ownership to her neighbors when her husband is not in the city. And even though if each and every [resident] gives bread, it appears that it is permitted even if they do not prohibit one another, as long as the husband did not protest — since presumably he does not object — nevertheless, one cannot rely on this with regard to her being able to transfer ownership to others. And if neither the husband [nor the] wife is in the city, but only members of his household, one must examine whether the members of his household can establish an eiruv without permission from [the property] of the homeowner; for shortly [on 80b] we learn in the Mishnah: "[If residents] were added to them, he adds [to the eiruv] and must notify [them]"; and when the food was depleted, it is also taught that he must notify [them if collecting] from a different type [of food].

Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:5:1.hebrew: רב אמר א"ל לזכות - דכיון דאסר עליה, גמר ומקני ליה; ובתחומין צריך לזכות, דלא אסר עליה ולא נמר ומקני, כדפירש בקונטרס. ולשמואל, במבוי צריך לזכות, דלמקני רשות הוא — דקסבר: עירוב משים קנין, בפ' מי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין דף מט.); אפילו למ"ד עירוב משום דירה, צריך לזכות כדי שיהא קונה דירה בבית חבירו. ובתחומין סבר שמואל דאין צריך לזכות, דלא קני רשות אחרים הוא. אי נמי, כיון דאין מערבין עירובי תחומין אלא לדבר מצוה, משום מצוה גמר ומקני. ועוד, כיון דעירובי תחומין אין מערבין אלא מדעתו, אמירתו כשהוא אומר "צא וערב לי" חשובה כזכייה. והשתא, יש דברים שאנו מחמירין בחצירות מתחומין: דחצירות צריך לזכות לשמואל ובפי פח, ובתחומין אין צריך לזכות ואין צריך פת; ויש דברים שאנו מחמירין בתחומין טפי: דבתחומין בעי ב' סעודות לכל אחד, ובחצירות, בזמן שהן מרובין סגי [במזון ב' סעודות לכולם, ובזמן שהן מועטין סגי] בגרוגרת לכל אחד, כדאמרינן סוף פירקין; והשולח עירוב ביד חרש, שוטה וקטן — אינו עירוב בתחומין, ובחצירות קטן גובה אח העירוב:
Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:5:1.english: Rav said: It is not necessary to confer possession - For since [each resident] restricts the other, he wholeheartedly transfers [possession of the food] to him; and regarding [the joining of Shabbat] boundaries, it is necessary to confer possession, for [one] does not restrict the other, and [so] he does not wholeheartedly transfer [possession], as Rashi explained. And according to Shmuel, in an alleyway it is necessary to confer possession, as it is to acquire rights in the domain — for he maintains that an eiruv is due to acquisition, in the chapter [entitled] "Mi Shehotzi’ohu" (above, Eruvin 49a); [and] even according to the one who says that an eiruv is due to dwelling, it is necessary to confer possession so that he will acquire a dwelling in his fellow's house. And regarding boundaries, Shmuel maintains that it is not necessary to confer possession, as it is not an acquisition of the domain of others. Alternatively: Since one may establish a joining of boundaries only for the purpose of a mitzvah, on account of the mitzvah he wholeheartedly transfers [possession]. And furthermore: Since one may establish a joining of boundaries only with his knowledge [and consent], his statement when he says "Go out and establish an eiruv for me" is considered like conferring possession. And now, there are matters in which we are more stringent regarding courtyards than boundaries: for [with regard to] courtyards, it is necessary to confer possession according to Shmuel, and [it must be] with bread [ubefat, misprinted ubefi pach]; whereas regarding boundaries, it is not necessary to confer possession, and it does not require bread. And there are matters in which we are more stringent regarding boundaries: for regarding boundaries, [the eiruv] requires [food for] two meals for each person; whereas regarding courtyards, when they are numerous, [food for] two meals for all of them suffices, [and when they are few, it suffices] with a dried fig for each person, as we say at the end of our chapter (80b); and one who sends an eiruv via a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor — it is not an [effective] eiruv regarding boundaries, whereas regarding courtyards, a minor may collect the eiruv [food].

Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:7:1.hebrew: מעשה בכלתו כו' - פי' בקונטרס דהאי עובדא בתחומין היה. ואע"ג דבחצירות פליגא מתני' עליה דרב — רב תנא הוא ופליג. וקשיא, דעיקר הקושיא לא היתה אלא מחצירות, ומהא לא משני מידי! וי"ל דבעירובי חצירות היה המעשה, וכן פירש רבינו חננאל; ורב סבר כרבי ישמעאל, וקסבר רב דתנא דיק תנא בחצירות דבעינן זיכוי — כל שכן בתחומין, דתחומין לכולי עלמא בעי זכיה. ולפירוש הקונטרס דמוקי לה בתחומין, יש לומר דרבי חייא ורבי ישמעאל בר' יוסי משום אביו אזדו לטעמייהו: דר' חייא אית ליה לפיל בספ"ק דתחומין דאורייתא, ולהכי מחמיר בהו; ור' יוסי דמיקל — לטעמיה, דאמר לעיל (עירובין דף צה.) ספק עירוב כשר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 80a:7:1.english: "An incident involving his daughter-in-law, etc." - Rashi explained that this incident was with regard to [an eiruv of Shabbat] boundaries. And even though regarding [an eiruv of] courtyards the Mishnah disagrees with Rav, Rav is a tanna and [has the authority to] disagree. But this is difficult, for the primary difficulty was only from [the mishnah regarding] courtyards, and from this [incident regarding boundaries] nothing is resolved! And it can be said that the incident was [actually] concerning an eiruv of courtyards, and so explained Rabbeinu Chananel; and Rav held in accordance with Rabbi Yishmael. And Rav maintained that the Tanna [of our mishnah] was precise: he taught regarding courtyards that we require conferring possession, [which applies] all the more so regarding boundaries, for with regard to boundaries everyone agrees that it requires conferring possession. And according to the explanation of Rashi, who establishes it as [an incident] regarding boundaries, it can be said that Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose in the name of his father followed their [established] reasoning: for Rabbi Chiyya holds above [reading le'eil instead of lefil] at the end of the first chapter (17b) that [the prohibition of leaving Shabbat] boundaries is of Torah origin, and therefore he is stringent regarding them; and Rabbi Yose, who is lenient, [acted] in accordance with his [established] reasoning, as he said earlier (35b; in printed editions: 95a): "An uncertain eiruv is valid."
